explanation: I found no Mathlib declaration that states this. The theorem says the library's own construction `rightFreeLinearMapScalarExtension` respects composition. That construction moves a right-linear map between free modules over R to one over S along a ring map `f : R →+* S`: it converts the map to a matrix through the library's `rightFreeCoordEquiv`, applies `f` to each entry with `Matrix.map`, and converts back. Mathlib has the pieces: `LinearMap.toMatrixRight'_comp` (the matrix of a composition is the product of the matrices) and `Matrix.map_mul` (applying a ring map to the entries preserves products). Getting this result from them, though, means unfolding the library's definition and its coordinate equivalences and combining several lemmas. The library's proof does it another way: it checks the maps on basis vectors (`Pi.single`) using its own lemmas. All the mathematical content sits in the library's own definition, so this is neither a duplicate nor a special case of a single Mathlib declaration.
